title: ⭐ Practice: talking about your work and offering an idea

questions.prompt: Complete: "What about ___ the new words with a partner every Friday?"
questions.explanation: "practising" is right: what about is followed by a noun or by a verb in -ing — What about practising the new words with a partner every Friday? "to practise" is the classic trap of this structure, which never takes to; "practise" is the base form, which belongs after why not, should or could; and "practised" is a past form that cannot follow about.

questions.prompt: Complete: "I'm not very good at ___ long words correctly."
questions.explanation: "pronouncing" is right: good at is followed by a noun or by a verb in -ing — I'm not very good at pronouncing long words correctly. "to pronounce" is the classic trap after at, "pronounce" is the bare base form and "pronounced" is a past form; at accepts none of the three.

questions.prompt: Complete: "You should ___ the words of every lesson."
questions.explanation: "revise" is right: should and could are followed by the base verb alone — You should revise the words of every lesson. "to revise" adds a to that these two structures never take, "revising" is the -ing form that belongs after what about, and "revises" carries the present -s that a base form never has.

questions.prompt: You and your partner have found the same strong point and the same difficulty. Which sentence reports both of them to the class?

options.text: I agree that my strong point is grammar and my difficulty is new words.
You agree that your strong point is grammar and your difficulty is new words.
They agree that their strong point is grammar and their difficulty is new words.
We agree that our strong point is grammar and our difficulty is new words.

questions.explanation: "We agree that our strong point is grammar and our difficulty is new words." is right: a conclusion that you and your partner share is reported with we and our. "I agree that my strong point is grammar and my difficulty is new words." gives your own point alone, "You agree that your strong point…" speaks to somebody instead of speaking for the pair, and "They agree that their strong point…" hands the conclusion to a third group outside it.

questions.prompt: Complete: "If you ___ more texts in English, you will meet the same words again."
questions.explanation: "read" is right: after if the verb stays in the present, and will belongs to the other half of the sentence — If you read more texts in English, you will meet the same words again. "will read" puts will in both halves, which this structure never does; "would read" belongs to a different kind of sentence; and "reads" adds an -s that never goes with you.

questions.prompt: Complete this resolution for the new term: "___ be more active in pair and group work."
questions.explanation: "I'll" is right: a resolution is will plus the base verb, and in speech and in notes I will is shortened to I'll — I'll be more active in pair and group work. "I'm" is the short form of I am, "I've" of I have and "I'd" of I would; none of the three announces a decision taken now for the future.
